# devhop
> Zero-config CLI that puts a local web dev server on a phone: a Cloudflare quick tunnel for trusted HTTPS plus a small proxy so dev servers accept the tunnel host. Hot reload, mic and camera access, and a terminal QR code.

- CLI: `npx devhop [target]` (Node.js 20 or newer)
- Repo: https://github.com/fullstacked-labs/devhop
- npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/devhop
- Docs: https://github.com/fullstacked-labs/devhop#readme
- Agent skill: https://github.com/fullstacked-labs/devhop/blob/main/skills/devhop/SKILL.md

## Tested frameworks
Checked nightly in CI (page loads and hot reload works through the tunnel, and the same checks fail without devhop): Vite 8 (React), Next.js 16, Nuxt 4, SvelteKit 3, Astro 7.

## Key Capabilities
- Vite-based servers answer 403 `Blocked request. This host ("...") is not allowed.` for the tunnel host; devhop rewrites Host, Origin and Referer to `localhost:<port>` so no `allowedHosts` edit is needed.
- Next.js 16 refuses the `/_next/hmr` WebSocket from a tunnel host (`allowedDevOrigins`); devhop makes hot reload work without that config.
- Trusted HTTPS gives Mobile Safari and Android Chrome a secure context for microphone and camera (`getUserMedia`), WebCrypto and Passkeys.
- Tolerant input parsing: accepts bare ports (`3000`), `host:port`, and HTTP(S) URLs such as `http://localhost:5173` or `https://localhost:8443`; a bare `443` implies HTTPS.
- Upstream HTTPS accepts self-signed certificates on loopback. A wrong scheme returns `502` with a hint to retry using the matching URL scheme.
- Prints a compact terminal QR code (`--no-qr` to skip).
- Mobile inspector: `https://<tunnel>/__devhop/inspect` provides an app preview iframe, a one-tap Eruda bookmarklet, and Vite/Next.js bundler recipes.
- Agent-ready: `--json` prints one JSON event per line on stdout (`ready` with `url`, `inspectUrl` and `edgeReady`; `reconnecting`; `error` with a stable `code`; `closed`) so coding agents can act on failures.
- `npx devhop --doctor` (add `--json` for a `doctor` event) prints diagnostics to paste into bug reports.
- Corporate firewall bypass: `--http2` routes the tunnel over HTTP/2 (TCP 443) when UDP/QUIC is blocked.
- cloudflared is downloaded once, pinned and checked against a SHA-256; set `DEVHOP_CLOUDFLARED=/path/to/cloudflared` to use your own binary.
- No account or signup.

## Limits
Quick tunnels are for testing: URLs are public and change every run, Server-Sent Events are not supported, and Cloudflare caps concurrent requests.
